- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Eiffel Tower is a wrought iron lattice tower located on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Eiffel Tower was named after the engineer Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and built the tower.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The construction of the Eiffel Tower began in 1887 and was completed in 1889 for the Exposition Universelle (World's Fair) celebrating the centennial of the French Revolution.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] At the time of its completion, the Eiffel Tower was the tallest structure in the world, standing at 1,063 feet (324 meters) tall.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Initially, the Eiffel Tower was not well received by the public, and many criticized its design as an eyesore.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Over time, the Eiffel Tower became an iconic symbol of Paris, and its popularity grew.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Eiffel Tower has had a significant impact on the tourism industry in Paris, becoming the most visited paid monument in the world, with over 7 million visitors annually.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The popularity of the Eiffel Tower has helped make Paris one of the top tourist destinations in the world.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Eiffel Tower has also played a role in scientific research and communication, being used for radio and television broadcasting, and as a platform for scientific experiments and astronomical observations.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Today, the Eiffel Tower remains one of the most recognizable landmarks in the world and continues to draw visitors from all over the globe.
